result.title: Feature-Based and Deep Learning Methods for Astronomical Light Curve Classification
result.comment: 14 pages, 5 figures. Submitted to Moscow University Physics Bulletin (DLCP-2026 special issue)
result.summary: We compare feature-based machine learning and end-to-end deep learning for variable star classification using the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) StarEmbed dataset, which contains about 40,000 objects across seven imbalanced classes. Classical models trained on physically motivated features consistently outperform deep networks trained directly on raw light curves. We find that limited labeled data contributes to the performance gap, while the multivariate, irregularly sampled, and morphologically diverse nature of light curves poses additional challenges for deep learning models. While deep learning holds promise for learning representations directly from observations, our results indicate that current models fail to generalize with the available training set size. These findings motivate further investigation of the benefits of scaling labeled datasets and self-supervised pretraining on large unlabeled surveys. This work establishes a quantitative baseline for future research and highlights the need for further innovations to unlock the potential of deep learning in astronomical time series analysis.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在 ZTF StarEmbed 变星数据集（约四万条、七类不平衡）上比较基于物理特征的传统机器学习与直接学习原始光变曲线的端到端深度模型，发现前者稳定更优，并将差距主要归因于标注数据有限及光变曲线不规则采样、形态多样的特点。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「人工设计特征 vs 端到端学习表示」及数据规模制约表示泛化的结论，可能与 LVR 中内部状态是否保留任务必要信息、latent 表示的数据效率问题形成类比，可供核查，但领域与模态相距较远。
